findings.text: the population gate recorded this test and tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py:1326 as added failures the reviewed manifest does not retire by name, so reckon/crew/review.py:1177 caps the review total at 5 on read; a focused head re-run of both passes (focused-head-rerun.log, 2 passed in 10.50s), showing they are contention artifacts of the -n 8 population arm rather than consequences of the change, but the reviewed run recorded neither that re-run nor an attribution for the ids under failure_attribution, so the artifact claim is the reviewer's, not the node's.

justifications.durability: all seven cases in tests/test_orchestrator_lane_fence.py fail against base 657e199ba (negative-control-base.log, 7 failed, EXIT=1), and test_removing_the_declaration_stops_the_fence_firing asserts state not-declared plus an empty warning list on the same node and lane with only the declaration removed -- an independent null control that reddens if the fence fires without reading the declaration.
justifications.evidence: the gate and its result are recorded -- after_suite over the importing population 2 failed/1941 passed (gate-population-head.log) and negative-control-base.log 7 failed at EXIT=1 -- but the done-when's population clause is unmet by two added failures the reviewed manifest does not retire by name and leaves unattributed, and the base arm was narrowed to three files rather than the full population, so the delta is not a clean whole-population comparison.
justifications.fit: the new symbols (ORCHESTRATOR_LANE_DECLARATION_KEY, ORCHESTRATOR_LANE_STOP_SEVERITY, _dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop) are named by mechanism with no plan label, the flight.yaml slot mirrors its siblings, and the record-reaches-the-pointer wiring at dispatch.py:7163 follows the lane_gate pattern at dispatch.py:7158.
